deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister's complexity argument by pointing out that hundreds of industry experts have already created a regulatory framework ready for Government adoption, asking her to acknowledge this preparatory work.

deb_ex.sum: Proposes equipping bin lorries with AI cameras to spot and map potholes in real time, urging cross-departmental coordination and funding to roll this out nationally.

deb_ex.t: Why can we not have emergency prison places rather than letting these dangerous people on to our streets to do more harm?
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether closed prisons could be reopened quickly and suggests emergency prison places modelled on Nightingale hospitals as an alternative to releasing dangerous offenders.

deb_ex.t: this is an occasion on which we might find common cause and seek a way forward
deb_ex.sum: Urges the Minister to take up the Opposition's offer of cross-party cooperation to find a solution to the prison numbers crisis that protects constituents from harm.

deb_ex.t: What is the purpose of a judge agreeing a sentence when the victims of the crime know that the person responsible for it will only serve half the time
deb_ex.sum: Makes a principled case for retributive justice and longer sentences, demands precise figures on how many rapists, child sex offenders and manslaughter convicts will be released early, and calls for cross-party talks to find a solution.

deb_ex.t: there were 870 notifications of serious further offences committed by released prisoners in 2024-25, including 56 murders and 107 rapes
deb_ex.sum: Cites official data showing 870 serious further offences by released prisoners including 56 murders and 107 rapes in 2024-25, and implores the Minister to pursue cross-party talks before further crimes are committed.

deb_ex.t: No party has a monopoly on wisdom. No Government get everything right. Governments make mistakes, as indeed do parties
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the Labour Member's call for cross-party co-operation, reflects on how MPs work across party lines on shared causes, and hopes the Minister will accept the offer of collaboration.

deb_ex.t: There are ways in which we could address the matter that would avoid our letting the most dangerous criminals on to the streets.
deb_ex.sum: Praises Mullan's advocacy for victims and argues there is an opportunity to exclude the most dangerous criminals from early release rather than letting them onto the streets.

deb_ex.t: one in eight prisoners is a foreign national taking up valuable prison space. There are 10,376 foreign national criminals in our prisons today
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the visa withdrawal proposal, cites the cost and scale of foreign national prisoners, and urges the Government to confirm it will not release violent offenders or child groomers.

deb_ex.t: the plan to release up to 6,000 criminals in September needs to be stalled, so that we can think again.
deb_ex.sum: Calls for the September release of up to 6,000 criminals to be stalled and argues that sex offenders, rapists, and those guilty of manslaughter or child grooming should be removed from the release list.

deb_ex.t: We need to know that more innocent people will not be put at risk. The very least we should do is deal with the issue of serious sexual offenders
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the Government's lack of clarity on who will be released, cites the case of Shabir Ahmed and Jade Belgrove, and demands Parliament send a clear message that dangerous offenders will not be freed.

deb_ex.t: The lack of faith that was bound to come from that reluctance will now be exaggerated—doubled—when these people are let out of prison
deb_ex.sum: Argues that releasing Pakistani-origin grooming gang members early will compound the existing loss of public faith caused by reluctance to acknowledge the ethnic dimension of the crimes.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that over-reliance on Chinese-processed materials for renewables is as dangerous as dependence on petrochemical dictators, and links energy policy failures to the malign influence of Iran and Russia.

deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to argue that today's debate was arranged to prevent scrutiny of the new Prime Minister and that contributions so far have not matched the urgency the Leader of the House claimed justified changing parliamentary business.

deb_ex.sum: Argues that vague government statements on oil and gas are insufficient, and demands exploitation of North Sea resources to deliver genuine energy security.

deb_ex.sum: Urges the Government to ensure the new laws are applied without fear or favour to elected councillors who have openly supported proscribed groups or spread disinformation, and condemns the firebombing of the Prime Minister's family home.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the pressure on off-grid distilleries from rising fuel costs and signals the government is considering temporarily suspending tariffs on kerosene oil.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely wish the hon. Member’s constituents all the best. It is entrepreneurial spirit like that that drives the economy forward. I will give one example of the support: there

deb_ex.t: That will give the UK the strongest legal framework on late payments in the G7.
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the Commercial Payments Bill, describing its provisions on payment terms, mandatory interest and enforcement powers as giving the UK the strongest G7 framework on late payments.

deb_ex.t: For too long, large businesses have used small businesses as a source of free credit. That will end under these plans.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Bill will require payment within 60 days with mandatory interest on late invoices, ending the practice of large businesses using small firms as free credit, and promises better cash flow and growth.

deb_ex.t: our small business strategy is improving access to markets for small businesses, improving access to finance for small businesses, and cutting the regulatory burden
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges a tough decade for small businesses and sets out the government's small business strategy covering markets, finance access, and regulatory burden reduction.

deb_ex.t: we have put significant resources into tackling the type of crime she raises. That is becoming a permanent approach under this Government.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the problem of bogus businesses and points to Operation Machinize and ongoing ministerial engagement with Companies House and the Insolvency Service as the government's response.

deb_ex.t: where there is a risk of disruption that does not mean the service will disappear
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the government's commitment to maintaining network size means closures will prompt searches for alternative sub-postmasters rather than permanent loss of service.

deb_ex.t: it was a reminder of the importance of our first employment experiences in making ourselves into fully rounded human beings and workers.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate for the Government, celebrating the value of summer jobs from personal experience while defending the Employment Rights Act and challenging Conservative claims about zero-hours contracts.

deb_ex.t: many people value flexibility in the workplace, but some employers have used that flexibility to take advantage of their employees, including young employees.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Employment Rights Act by arguing Conservative Members were defending zero-hours contracts that employers have used to exploit young workers.

deb_ex.t: where people genuinely value that flexibility in the workplace, they will be able to continue to work in that way.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the summer school group and clarifies that the Employment Rights Act does not force seasonal contracts to become permanent, defending Government policy.

deb_ex.t: hundreds of people in his constituency do not have the right to regular hours
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's zero-hours contract reforms by arguing workers who prefer flexibility can keep their arrangements, while those relying on such contracts as their main job deserve income certainty.

deb_ex.t: Maybe he can say why he thinks those hundreds of workers in his constituency should not have the right to full-time employment.
deb_ex.sum: Invites the Conservative Member to explain why workers in his constituency should be denied the right to full-time employment, pressing him to justify opposition to the reforms.

deb_ex.t: Those people will still be able to have those contracts under the legislation, but we are talking about potentially hundreds of people in the right hon. Member’s constituency—that
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's employment and business rates reforms, arguing zero-hours contract changes protect the most vulnerable workers and the youth guarantee package offsets national insurance costs for employers of young people.

deb_ex.t: we are dealing with the issue of youth unemployment by incentivising businesses to employ young people
deb_ex.sum: Defends government policy by emphasising incentives for businesses to hire young people and commits to reducing administrative burdens as part of a net target.

deb_ex.t: This Labour Government will act, and these reforms will deliver the national renewal that our country needs.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate defending the government's employment law reforms, business rates changes, and youth unemployment review, dismissing Conservative proposals as outdated.

deb_ex.t: A key priority for the new board will be looking at ways to reduce costs, and a huge part of that will be investing to help with energy costs.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees that past inaction harmed steelmaking communities and outlines existing energy cost interventions, noting that reducing costs will be a key priority for the new board.

deb_ex.t: Crude production has fallen by 50% over the last 10 years, and we have seen community after community abandoned.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister defends the decision as being in the national interest, not targeted at China, and rejects the Opposition's framing by pointing out that crude steel production fell 50% under the previous Government.

deb_ex.t: The blast furnaces on the site will continue for some time to come.

deb_ex.t: This morning, the workers on the site have been briefed on the decision.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister stresses the decision's importance to national security and infrastructure, and confirms workers on site have been briefed this morning with the new board expected to remain closely engaged.

deb_ex.t: the partnership comes with significant resources on the table, through the National Wealth Fund, to help the steel industry become more competitive, particularly on energy efficiency.

deb_ex.t: 80% of the rails we will be travelling on are made by British Steel.

deb_ex.t: The blast furnaces at Scunthorpe will be operational for the immediate term.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister reaffirms the steel strategy's preference for electric arc technology as the most competitive future, confirms blast furnaces will remain operational in the near term, and says the new board will address longer-term questions.

deb_ex.t: Without the measures we took, there was a real prospect of our becoming the global dumping ground for uncompetitively subsidised over-production.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister defends the safeguard measures as necessary to prevent the UK becoming a dumping ground, points to transitional arrangements and a 12-month review, and notes ongoing work with the EU on mutual arrangements.

deb_ex.t: As the Minister for Industry has set out, on the issue of cost, it is our intention to continue with the practice under the previous Act of coming to Parliament on a quarterly basi
deb_ex.sum: The Minister commits to quarterly written ministerial statements on costs and says the new board will be accountable to Select Committees.

deb_ex.t: through the work we are doing on public procurement, we are ensuring that there is a clearer line of sight for British steel producers
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms government investment to reduce costs and explains how public procurement guidance will give British Steel a fair chance at infrastructure contracts.

deb_ex.t: the clean industry bonus scheme—for offshore wind, for example—will incentivise its use.

deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question with light humour about ministerial continuity but assures the House that the Minister for Industry intends to update Parliament on the new board's strategic objectives.

deb_ex.t: We are deeply committed and open to private sector partnerships to ensure the future of British Steel, and that is an essential and early part of the conversation.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges nationalisation was a reluctant decision, notes the company has only been publicly owned for hours, and reaffirms openness to private sector partnerships for British Steel's future.

deb_ex.sum: Commits to the suggested meetings with Northern Ireland stakeholders, points to existing trade measure provisions for steel flow into Northern Ireland, and stresses the importance of continued dialogue with the EU.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the hawkish consensus by arguing that poverty and inequality are the real threats facing citizens, and calls for investment in public services and diplomacy rather than weapons.

deb_ex.t: diplomacy and international law are in tatters
deb_ex.sum: Condemns US-Israeli military strikes as illegal and argues the Trump administration is dismantling international law. Warns of catastrophic consequences for ordinary Iranians and calls for diplomacy over force.

deb_ex.t: The UK must join the moral and principled calls for an immediate and lasting ceasefire, to be followed by a swift resumption of negotiations.
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the Labour government for cutting overseas development aid and calls on the UK to demand an immediate ceasefire in Iran, denounce Trump's tactics, and affirm that Iran's future belongs to its own people.

deb_ex.sum: Endorses the previous speaker and argues that Trump and Netanyahu's actions are driven by imperialist and capitalist motives, not by any genuine desire to liberate the Iranian people.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms NHS trusts must have business continuity plans for adverse weather and that the Department works closely with NHS England and UKHSA, acknowledging this is an increasingly pressing issue.

deb_ex.sum: Responds by citing the 10-year health plan's prevention focus and a new duty on authorities to consider air quality, and offers to meet the MP.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's commitment to making this the healthiest generation of children, citing investment in family hubs, mental health support, and tobacco legislation.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the local initiatives highlighted by the hon. Member and notes they complement government prevention work, including a £1 billion investment in PE and school sport.

deb_ex.sum: Minister praises the Darren Deady Foundation and accepts the invitation to visit, noting his personal connection as an Afghan veteran.

deb_ex.t: One veteran rough sleeping is one too many. This Government will always ensure that support is available when needed.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government commitments on veteran homelessness, including £12 million for the reducing veteran homelessness programme and Op Fortitude support services.

deb_ex.t: Op Fortitude has helped more than 1,000 veterans into housing.
deb_ex.sum: Responds by outlining cross-government work with MHCLG and local authorities, exemptions from local connection rules for social housing, and the success of Op Fortitude in housing over 1,000 veterans.

deb_ex.t: the Catterick integrated care centre will open in Richmondshire later this year. This cutting-edge healthcare facility is a joint MOD and NHS initiative, the first of its kind
deb_ex.sum: Announces the forthcoming opening of the Catterick integrated care centre, a joint MOD-NHS facility serving both military and civilian communities in Richmondshire.

deb_ex.t: I would love to visit the facility with him so that we can highlight it as an exemplar that could be transferred to other parts of the country.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the facility should be an exemplar for other parts of the country and offers to visit it with Sunak to promote the model.

deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights his personal cadet background and sets out the government's commitment to expanding cadet forces by 30%, with the target to be met by 2035 and an action plan due in October.

deb_ex.sum: Rejects the characterisation that funding has been cut and reaffirms the government's target to expand cadet forces by 40,000 by 2035, directing the hon. Member to the cadet action plan.

deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly to the question about sea cadets, directing the hon. Member to the cadet action plan and offering a personal meeting to discuss the issues.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights the government's world-leading blast injury support, £3.65 million scanning technology investment and over £25 million in Op Courage since the election to support veterans' mental health.

deb_ex.t: I emphasise that £300 billion is new money; £15 billion is new money

deb_ex.sum: Attributes current capability risks directly to the 2010 removal of Nimrod and reduction of shipyards under the previous Conservative government.

deb_ex.t: UK defence spending will rise in real terms by 27% between 2023-24 and 2029-30—the largest sustained increase since the cold war
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's programme of defence investment, reform and NATO collaboration, arguing the DIP represents the largest sustained spending increase since the cold war.

deb_ex.t: Britain has always met its NATO spending obligations in the past, and under this Government we always will.
deb_ex.sum: Draws on his military service to affirm backing for the defence investment plan and pledges the government will meet NATO spending obligations, starting with raising defence investment to 2.7% of GDP.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes his colleague's long-standing advocacy for the DSR Bank and notes recent announcements on the bank and the multilateral defence mechanism, expressing hope the two will be aligned.

deb_ex.t: The DIP will energise the transformation of our armed forces and target resources to reflect how war is waged today.
deb_ex.sum: Argues the DIP will drive transformation through AI, autonomy and uncrewed systems, and defends the autonomous Navy programme as coherent and cost-effective against a critic, citing Portsmouth evidence.

deb_ex.t: at the moment we are providing 150,000 drones a year to Ukraine.

deb_ex.t: We say thank you to every member of our military in the middle east, saving lives and working with international partners to defend our interests.
deb_ex.sum: Concludes tribute to British military personnel in the Middle East, expressing national pride in their service.

deb_ex.t: We want to see a diplomatic solution to this crisis. We call for the resumption of a ceasefire and for the United States and Iran to resume negotiations
deb_ex.sum: Defends ministerial attendance, outlines Iranian attacks on shipping and allies, and sets out the Government's unchanged objectives of diplomacy, ceasefire and freedom of navigation.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the cyber threat, outlines reinforcement of regional partners' air defences, deployment of HMS Dragon, and warns of economic consequences of conflict in the strait of Hormuz.

deb_ex.t: Our security services tracked more than 20 potentially lethal Iran-backed plots on British soil between October 2024 and October 2025, targeting journalists, dissidents and Jewish people
deb_ex.sum: Explains HMS Dragon's current UK-led role with potential to join a broader French-led mission, and outlines Iran-backed terror plots on British soil and recent sanctions including on HAYI.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for her powerful intervention. It is important to note that that regime does not respect freedom of religion. Back here at home, every one of us, regardless
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the Iranian regime does not respect freedom of religion and calls on everyone to stand up for others regardless of faith.

deb_ex.sum: Receives the DUP Member's questions graciously and promises fuller answers in closing remarks.

deb_ex.t: any nation that poses such a terror threat abroad, that murders thousands of its own people and brutally suppresses dissent at home, must never acquire a nuclear weapon
deb_ex.sum: Agrees all must be present and contribute to debates on division, and reaffirms that Iran must never acquire a nuclear weapon.

deb_ex.t: nations that are acting within our country to cause division between people and communities and to attack our democracy and our state
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the domestic threat from Iranian state actors seeking to divide communities and attack democracy, and warns of Iran's nuclear stockpile far exceeding JCPOA limits while offering UK assistance in achieving a verifiable deal.

deb_ex.t: to encourage the resumption of negotiations and a ceasefire; to restore freedom of movement in the strait of Hormuz; to deliver the agreements set out in the memorandum of understanding
deb_ex.sum: Closes his opening speech by restating the Government's four core priorities: resuming negotiations, restoring freedom of navigation, delivering the MOU and protecting British people and allies.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Opposition's criticism of the DIP by pointing to the previous Conservative government's equipment plan funding deficit and the £298 billion committed under the current plan.

deb_ex.sum: Accepts the criticism of victim notification letters and commits to further correspondence and improved engagement with victims throughout the process.

deb_ex.t: if the Sentencing Act measures are not implemented, in October or November of this year we will be back where we were in July 2024
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's decision not to divide on the Opposition day motion, warns that halting the Sentencing Act would recreate the prison capacity crisis, and reiterates commitment to balancing safety with sustainability.

deb_ex.t: the Opposition party has no plan for how to deal with the prison crisis that its amendment would have brought about later this year
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Opposition's cross-party offer as hollow given they have no credible plan for prison capacity, and pledges that by the end of this Parliament more criminals will be behind bars than ever under Labour.

deb_ex.t: We are ramping up tagging to monitor offenders in the community, with thousands more subject to 24/7 monitoring and curfews

deb_ex.t: either strict licence conditions in the community for those who have already served time in prison under the changes; or, simply put, the collapse of the system altogether
deb_ex.sum: Argues that the choice is between managed licence conditions for those who have already served time or total system collapse, and highlights new victim rights under the Victims and Courts Act 2026.

deb_ex.t: Every offender has a level of dangerousness, which is risk-assessed by probation as and when they leave prison
deb_ex.sum: States that dangerousness is already assessed by judges and probation for every offender and closes by defending the government's prison-building and sentencing reform programme.

deb_ex.t: Order. Sorry, but you’ve gone way over your one minute. I think your border queue has just gone. I call the Minister.

deb_ex.t: thank you for all that you have done

deb_ex.sum: The Speaker pays personal tribute to the late Ann Widdecombe, praising her principles and courage, while urging Members to avoid comments that could prejudice any future trial.

deb_ex.sum: The Speaker reassures the House that he treats the security of every Member equally and that all concerns brought to his attention are passed on to security staff.

deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the significance of the 2010 apology and commits to honouring its legacy alongside today's new apology.

deb_ex.t: All of these injustices build on the initial injustice, and they are not all so historical, either; some of them are much more contemporary.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that secondary injustices compound the original wrong and commits to addressing them with eyes wide open, noting some are not historical but contemporary.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the need for tangible, streamlined action and commits to working with devolved administrations to avoid adding further injustice.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that campaigners deserve full credit and reflects on the state's responsibility, saying their work was not heeded quickly enough.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that all affected must be heard and seen, including mothers, adult adoptees, extended families and those who have passed away.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges that the apology provides justice but does not remove pain, and commits to continuing support for all those affected.

deb_ex.t: The work to get us here today has been done in conjunction with all those affected, and we will continue to work in that way.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms that work was done in conjunction with those affected and commits to continuing that collaborative approach to address remaining challenges.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks the MP for raising those points and commits to working with her and others to put appropriate support, screening and information in place.

deb_ex.sum: Sets a four-minute speaking limit, pays personal tribute to Sir David Amess and thanks her constituency team.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on NHS dentistry, citing 2.5 million additional treatments and improved appointment rates, and promises further fundamental reform.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely accept his point that we still have a long way to go to get NHS dentistry back on its feet.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges there is still a long way to go on NHS dentistry, explains ICB responsibilities for commissioning, and agrees to meet the MP to discuss local concerns.

deb_ex.t: it is a bit rich to be given lectures from the Conservative party, which had 14 years to fix NHS dentistry and did absolutely nothing about it.
deb_ex.sum: Deflects Conservative criticism by highlighting 14 years of Tory inaction and reaffirms the government's commitment to fundamental dental contract reform, with a public consultation launching soon.

deb_ex.t: The fundamental problem is that dentists have not been incentivised to do NHS work. When we came into office in July 2024, we had a crazy situation where there was a £392 million u
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's record, explaining they inherited a £392 million underspend that has been reduced to £30 million and have delivered 2.5 million additional NHS dental treatment courses.

deb_ex.t: We are rapidly working to deliver our commitment of 120 NHCs by 2030 and 250 by 2035.
deb_ex.sum: Explains that ICB proposals have been reviewed and reaffirms the commitment to deliver 120 neighbourhood health centres by 2030 and 250 by 2035, with locations based on local need and health inequality.

deb_ex.t: Our modern service framework will transform palliative care by basing it on strategic commissioning
deb_ex.sum: Sets out how the modern service framework will transform palliative care through strategic commissioning and agrees to meet the hon. Member and Baroness Finlay.

deb_ex.t: Dementia is a vital issue, and we are of course committed to creating a national care service. Baroness Casey’s independent commission will set out recommendations to deliver that.
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the government's commitment to a national care service and outlines steps already underway including Baroness Casey's commission and the creation of a dementia tsar.

deb_ex.t: I would be delighted to meet him to follow up. It sounds as if some progress is being made
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he has discussed the issue with the hon. Member and agrees to a follow-up meeting to help resolve the situation.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the need to repeal and replace the 2023 Act, which lacked cross-community support, and expresses confidence the new Bill will be fair and balanced.

deb_ex.sum: Defers the specific amendment to Committee stage and reaffirms the long-established principle that national security responsibility rests with Ministers while committing to maximum disclosure.

deb_ex.t: I hope that we will see co-operation in response to the requests that the Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery is making of the Irish Government.
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Irish Government's published legislative outline and the Dillon judgment as grounds for expecting fuller Irish co-operation with the commission's information requests.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the Bill's information-sharing provisions are precisely the answer to the DUP's concerns and reaffirms that is a central reason to proceed with the legislation.

deb_ex.t: given the recent serious disorder, there is a problem that needs to be tackled.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he regularly meets the Northern Ireland Executive and PSNI on community cohesion and acknowledges recent serious disorder as a problem requiring action.

deb_ex.t: nurses described to me how, because of the colour of their skin, they were too afraid to leave the hospital at the end of their shift
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the condemnation, shares harrowing accounts from hospital nurses too afraid to leave work due to racist thuggery, and says the events should give cause for deep concern.

deb_ex.t: there is no doubt that part of the violence was fuelled by that kind of online hatred.
deb_ex.sum: Explains that far-right groups used a publicly available Belfast council list to target houses and stresses that social media companies and Ofcom have clear obligations under the Online Safety Act to tackle online hatred that fuelled the vi

deb_ex.t: political leaders have a responsibility to call out what was witnessed for what it is and not mince our words
deb_ex.sum: Sets out shared responsibilities across political leaders, social media companies, police, community organisations and parents for calling out and preventing racist violence in Belfast.

deb_ex.t: there is now another other: the ethnic minority population of Northern Ireland, who are terrified about what is happening.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges Northern Ireland's ongoing post-Good Friday Agreement journey of shared history but differing memory, and warns that ethnic minority communities are now terrified and must not become a new target of division.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to raise this issue, because five of the main parties have now come forward with various proposals for reform. I have said to the party leaders that I wish
deb_ex.sum: Confirms willingness to meet party leaders on institutional reform proposals, notes budget pressures are currently absorbing effort, and highlights new PSNI powers to remove paramilitary flags.

deb_ex.t: There is a responsibility, above all, on the Northern Ireland Executive to deliver for the people of Northern Ireland.
deb_ex.sum: Places responsibility on the Northern Ireland Executive to deliver, notes that prolonged Executive absence has hindered progress, and links community stability to resolving the acute housing and water infrastructure crisis.

deb_ex.t: About 1,000 people who had no right to be in Northern Ireland have been removed, including 500 who have been returned to the Republic of Ireland.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights increased operations and arrests, removal of around 1,000 people with no right to be in Northern Ireland, and points to intelligence-led policing under Operation Gull at ports and workplaces.

deb_ex.t: I regularly meet representatives of the logistics sector and businesses trading between Great Britain and Northern Ireland—for instance, through the Northern Ireland business stake
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he regularly meets the logistics sector and businesses to discuss making the Windsor Framework operate as smoothly as possible.

deb_ex.t: if things are as bad as he suggests, why is Northern Ireland one of the fastest-growing parts of the United Kingdom economy?
deb_ex.sum: Defends the carbon charge on ferry routes as protecting Northern Ireland businesses from the carbon border adjustment mechanism, and challenges Wilson's negative characterisation by pointing to Northern Ireland's strong economic growth.

deb_ex.t: I met the leaders of the main Northern Ireland political parties on Thursday 11 June to discuss the terrible disorder. The attack on Mr Ogilvie was truly shocking, but the racist v
deb_ex.sum: Reports meeting Northern Ireland party leaders to discuss the disorder and condemns both the original attack and the racist violence that followed.

deb_ex.t: The single most important thing that we can all do as political leaders is to be absolutely clear that everyone who has made the United Kingdom their home lawfully should be treate
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that everyone lawfully living in the UK deserves equality, respect and dignity regardless of origin, presenting this as the most important message political leaders can send.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to my hon. Friend for what she says, and I agree with her. There was terrible disorder in Ballymena last year, as a result of which a number of steps were taken to br
deb_ex.sum: Points to Ballymena as an example of community trust-building after disorder, noting it was not repeated there, and calls for more such community work.

deb_ex.t: I hope the hon. Lady will recognise that the common travel area, which is more than a century old, is of great benefit to the citizens of the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ire
deb_ex.sum: Defends the common travel area as beneficial to citizens on both sides of the border, rules out border immigration controls as unrealistic, and cites 1,000 removals since the election including 500 to the Republic.

deb_ex.t: I join the hon. Gentleman in thanking and praising the brave officers of the PSNI. My hon. Friend the Member for Wirral West (Matthew Patrick) and I visited the officers at Strandt
deb_ex.sum: Joins in praising PSNI officers, notes the injuries sustained during the disorder, and promises further discussion on the new training centre.

deb_ex.t: There is equal treatment for all in work that we do on security for Members of Parliament.
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary agrees to discuss potential amendments to the Representation of the People Bill and assures the House that security provision is treated equally for all Members and is based on independent risk assessment.

deb_ex.t: My right hon. Friend is right to say that the climate in which we are operating in our national politics is unlike any that most of us have seen. Those of us who have been around f
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary agrees the political climate has changed markedly, acknowledges social media platforms must take greater responsibility, and commits to cross-government discussions on how to respond.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Lady makes an important point on the consequences for the Prevent duty of the changing nature of the threat. It is essential that we retain a deradicalisation progra
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary acknowledges that the changing nature of threats poses questions for the Prevent strategy and commits to reviewing the Committee's recommendations on radicalisation.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely give that assurance to my hon. Friend. I will pick up discussions with Mr Speaker and others on how we think about security for those who are no longer Members of this

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman has made a very moving and affecting tribute to Ann Widdecombe. On Widders whisky, as a teetotal Muslim, I would never be able to partake of such a drink, but if
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary responds warmly to the tribute, assures the Member that no lines of inquiry have been ruled out, and confirms that Devon and Cornwall police worked closely with counter-terrorism police before the handover.

deb_ex.t: We would not, of course, ever comment on the specific nature of the arrangements made for the security of Members of Parliament, either here on the estate or in their homes or cons
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary assures the Member that comprehensive arrangements are in place, while acknowledging the need to keep them under review in light of changing threats and the current spike in threat activity.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that we consider the privacy and security of home addresses.
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary accepts the point about home address privacy and commits to considering it in her lessons-learned work following Ann Widdecombe's murder.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right that we must ensure that people are not either driven out of politics or put off entering political life at all. It is incumbent on us all to work together
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary assures the Member that counter-terrorism police have the resources they need and reaffirms the Government's commitment to ensuring people are not deterred from entering public life.

deb_ex.t: we all have to do much more to hold social media companies to account for what is said and done through their platforms
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that society and government must do more to hold social media companies accountable, distinguishing fierce debate from threats and abuse, and calls for collective cross-party action on regulation.

deb_ex.t: we will do everything we can to protect the norms by which our democracy is felt across the country
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the Government's commitment to protecting democratic norms via the defending democracy taskforce and promises to engage with colleagues on amendments to the Representation of the People Bill.

deb_ex.t: People should exercise caution before they comment on this case—that is the right way to behave for those who wish to see justice done
deb_ex.sum: Calls on everyone to avoid speculation about the case, explains that police are constrained in what they can release, and urges the House to send out a clear message about expectations.

deb_ex.t: I shall discuss this matter with colleagues on a cross-party basis, and I will speak with Mr Speaker and the House authorities
deb_ex.sum: Promises to take up the issue of media publishing home details of Members and former Members in cross-party discussions and with Mr Speaker and the House authorities.

deb_ex.t: we must now live up to our responsibilities to former Members of Parliament as well
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the tribute, affirms the Government's serious duty toward the security of both current and former MPs, and states it must not be the case that serving in the House increases the risk of a violent death.

deb_ex.t: we as a society have to take a stronger position on the right boundary between contested debate and unacceptable behaviour and abuse online
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government will work closely with Mr Speaker and the Parliamentary Security Department and stresses the need for society to draw a firmer line between contested debate and unacceptable online behaviour.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that the House is updated soon after the summer recess
deb_ex.sum: Commits to cross-government discussions, specifically with DSIT, on regulating harmful social media behaviours and promises to update the House after the summer recess.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for that contribution. He will know that colleagues in DSIT are working carefully on the Online Safety Act 2023 and its further implementation, learning less
deb_ex.sum: Points to DSIT's work on implementing the Online Safety Act, commits to cross-government discussion on strengthening the boundary of acceptable online behaviour, and vows to update the House on the programme of work.

deb_ex.t: That was a very moving and funny set of memories from the right hon. Gentleman—very affecting. “Keep calm and carry on” are definitely words to live by, and we could all do with ta
deb_ex.sum: Warmly receives the tribute and memories of Ann Widdecombe and echoes best wishes to the police in their investigation.

deb_ex.t: I urge everyone, wherever they may sit on the political spectrum, to exercise calm and careful judgment before hitting the send button on social media messages
deb_ex.sum: Shares revulsion at denigrating comments about Ann Widdecombe and urges everyone across the political spectrum to pause and reflect before posting on social media.

deb_ex.t: I am sure we will have to go further. As I have committed before, I will make sure the House is updated in due course
deb_ex.sum: Places on record gratitude for counter-terrorism police, agrees with members' points about social media platform unaccountability, and commits to updating the House on further government action.

deb_ex.sum: Reflects on how her own advice surgeries have had to change since the murders of Jo Cox and Sir David Amess, agrees the connection between MPs and constituents is precious, and affirms the Government's determination to preserve good British

deb_ex.sum: Urges all Members to moderate their language toward colleagues, states any harassment by MPs of other MPs is unacceptable, confirms no specific threat to Reform UK MPs of which she is aware, and offers the Reform leader a meeting with RAVEC

deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's position by emphasising the independent, non-political nature of RAVEC's risk assessments and declines to comment on specific cases, assuring the House that operational independence will be maintained.

deb_ex.t: this country also cannot do without the work of its local councillors, parish councillors and all the people who put in the hours to make their local area better
deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly, acknowledging the risk to local councillors as well as parliamentarians, and confirms the Government is learning lessons from the defending democracy taskforce and Operation Ford with further developments expected.

deb_ex.t: this Government have begun the work of restoring order to our borders. That starts by taking the fight to the criminal gangs.
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary moves Second Reading, setting out the chaos inherited from the Conservatives, progress made on enforcement and asylum decisions, and the case for the Bill to restore fairness and control to the asylum system.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for what he said. He is absolutely right: we need to reduce the pressure in local communities as much as possible. He knows that dispersal accommodation has
deb_ex.sum: Agrees dispersal accommodation pressure must fall and argues the best way to achieve that is reducing small boat arrivals, which is the Bill's purpose.

deb_ex.t: around 94,000 people remain in asylum accommodation at a total cost of £3.7 billion per year
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question about her future role and returns to the scale of the remaining challenge, including 94,000 people in asylum accommodation and continued channel deaths.

deb_ex.t: there is a moral responsibility on all of us to think about how we deal with the particular challenge of small boats crossing the channel
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that channel deaths receive too little attention, argues there is a moral responsibility to stop the trade, and frames the Bill as essential to preserving public consent for asylum.

deb_ex.sum: Says earned settlement policy will be settled later this year following the consultation and notes it is not the subject of the Bill.

deb_ex.t: I remind my hon. Friend that, as he knows, we have paused family reunification, and the Government have said that we will bring forward further proposals for our approach to that.
deb_ex.sum: Reminds her colleague that family reunification is paused and further proposals are coming, and argues the current system lacks coherence and fairness across different migrant categories.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right. When people arrive through controlled, safe routes, when we have made a decision to allow people to enter, and when we are in control and not th
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that controlled, legal routes unlock the British public's generosity and frames community sponsorship as the foundation of the Government's asylum approach.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right—yes, they can and they do. That is the difference with a safe and legal route that has buy-in from communities across the country, and that is th
deb_ex.sum: Agrees community sponsorship schemes work and affirms they will be the basis for the future asylum system.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the new student refugee, community sponsorship and business sponsorship routes opening from autumn, with first arrivals in 2027, and explains how numbers will grow as illegal routes are reduced.

deb_ex.t: it has been settled Government policy to increase the qualifying period from five years to 10 years since last summer—since before I was Home Secretary
deb_ex.sum: Defends settled Government policy on the ILR qualifying period increase and confirms the earned settlement consultation on transitional arrangements will conclude in due course.

deb_ex.t: When we have settled policy later this year, those changes will be subject to the usual procedure for changes to immigration rules
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the Bill concerns asylum, human rights and appeals only, and that ILR changes will follow the standard immigration rules procedure with full parliamentary scrutiny.

deb_ex.t: I will give way to the right hon. Lady, but I will make progress after that.
deb_ex.sum: Indicates she will take one more intervention before making progress with her speech.

deb_ex.t: I say to the right hon. Lady, for whom I have the greatest respect, that it is not as if I am about to forget my own background, so I do not really need other people to remind me o
deb_ex.sum: Pushes back firmly on Abbott's intervention, notes her own background, and refocuses on breaking the people-smuggling trade by shifting to controlled safe and legal routes.

deb_ex.t: others have been made simply to delay a legitimate removal from this country
deb_ex.sum: Disagrees with critics of the appeals reforms, arguing that non-legally qualified decision makers operate across many tribunals and that the appeals queue is being gamed to delay legitimate removals.

deb_ex.t: A person does not have to be a judge to have good judgment.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the new independent immigration appeals authority staffed by adjudicators rather than judges, arguing this will provide greater capacity and flexibility than the current judicial model.

deb_ex.t: 50% of a 150,000 backlog is still 75,000 cases
deb_ex.sum: Responds that even 50% of a 150,000 backlog is a vast number and defends the single appeal route as targeting behaviours designed to frustrate lawful removal.

deb_ex.t: Our adjudicators will be paid professionals who are trained to make robust, defensible decisions.
deb_ex.sum: Details the new adjudicator structure, including a smaller cohort of legally trained adjudicators and an upper tribunal appeal on points of law, arguing decisions will be robust and defensible.

deb_ex.t: its decisions will be entirely independent of Government, with every Minister of the Crown compelled to uphold the independence of the authority
deb_ex.sum: Insists the new authority will be fully independent of government, with ministers compelled to uphold that independence, and explains the appointment process.

deb_ex.sum: Briefly invites a colleague who has not yet spoken to put a question.

deb_ex.t: All such appointments will be subject to the usual public appointments principles, which will apply here as they do elsewhere.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms appointments will follow standard public appointments principles and offers to discuss additional safeguards with Members as the Bill progresses.

deb_ex.t: I have given way to my hon. Friend before; I will make progress and come back to him. In the new system, a single, faster appeal route will be established, as addressed in clauses
deb_ex.sum: Explains the single appeal route that requires claimants to raise all matters upfront, with an expedited process for late claims, and introduces the core protection model replacing two overlapping statuses.

deb_ex.t: I will give way to my hon. Friend the Member for Edinburgh East and Musselburgh
deb_ex.sum: Briefly manages contributions from colleagues before taking the next intervention.

deb_ex.t: I think my hon. Friend means mandatory reconsideration in the context of a case when an appeal is made.
deb_ex.sum: Seeks to clarify her colleague's point about mandatory reconsideration in the context of an appeal.

deb_ex.t: before a case proceeds to appeal, we already have an internal process whereby we check whether we should still defend the claim at appeal stage
deb_ex.sum: Explains that an internal checking process already exists before cases proceed to appeal and expresses reluctance to add further bureaucratic layers.

deb_ex.t: he kept putting in appeal after appeal after appeal after appeal. These reforms are designed to deal with that problem.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the need to improve initial decision quality but insists multiple reforms are needed simultaneously, and uses the example of a foreign national offender's repeated appeals to justify the single appeal route.

deb_ex.t: last-minute claims have been made by a convicted rapist, a gangster jailed for possession of a firearm, and an attempted murderer
deb_ex.sum: Details measures strengthening modern slavery protections for children while addressing abuse of the system, including exclusion of those posing public order risks and penalising late disclosures.

deb_ex.sum: Concludes the second reading speech by summarising the Bill's aims: fast and fair decisions, genuine refugee protection, closing human rights loopholes, and introducing a contributory repayment principle for asylum support.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms detailed design work has commenced following the spending review decision but cannot give a specific start date, noting new train services should come on line in the 2030s.

deb_ex.sum: Outlines government action including a new mass transit taskforce, a call for evidence, and devolution of powers to local leaders to speed up delivery.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges cross-boundary transport challenges and points to the 'Better Connected' strategy, expressing confidence that Yorkshire's elected representatives will work together for the best outcomes.

deb_ex.t: The Fair Dealing Obligations (Pigs) Regulations 2025 are ending unfair contract practices, with all pre-existing contracts required to be compliant by 13 August.
deb_ex.sum: Minister sets out government action on pig sector supply chains, citing the Fair Dealing Obligations Regulations 2025 as delivering fairer contracts and greater producer protections.

deb_ex.t: We will ensure fairer, more transparent contracts to build a resilient and profitable industry.
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges challenges facing pig farmers and restates government commitment to fairer, more transparent contracts to build a resilient and profitable industry.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his engagement on this matter. The pig sector is vital to British farming, and I know from my time with him at the Royal Norfolk show the other week that
deb_ex.sum: Thanks his colleague for championing the sector and confirms he has accepted the National Pig Association's invitation to meet and discuss industry challenges.

deb_ex.t: Baroness Hayman in the other place has visited the port to understand the issues that he describes. We take these issues extremely seriously.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the border biosecurity concerns raised, notes a ministerial visit to the port, and offers to meet the shadow Minister to discuss the issues further.

deb_ex.t: The Government secured a major increase in the UK’s annual bluefin tuna quota from 63 tonnes to around 230 tonnes, creating new opportunities for fishers across the United Kingdom.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position: a major quota increase was secured and licences were allocated through a fair, transparent ballot process, with ongoing work with devolved governments.

deb_ex.t: As my hon. Friend rightly says, one Scottish fisher secured a commercial bluefin tuna licence in 2025, authorised through a fair and transparent application process. That fisher wa
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the Scottish fisher's unsuccessful 2026 application, explains licences are issued year by year due to demand, and commits to considering the hon. Member's ideas while working with Scottish fisheries administrations.

deb_ex.t: I thank him for his invitation to engage in these issues and I am happy to follow up with him.
deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly to the hon. Member's invitation, references a previous Westminster Hall debate, and commits to following up on Northern Ireland fisheries issues.

deb_ex.t: I take those issues seriously and I want to ensure that there is certainty and clarity in the sector.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms an upcoming meeting with the National Pig Association, notes the farming road map provides certainty, and offers to follow up on the concerns about independent pig producers.

deb_ex.t: We want people to know where their food comes from, trust what they are buying, and back British farmers who meet our high standards.
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the principle of clearer food origin labelling for consumers and farmers and offers to meet the MP to discuss his proposals.

deb_ex.t: I take these issues extremely seriously, and will bring forward the meeting so that I see the organisation as soon as possible.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the committee chair and commits to bringing forward a meeting with the National Pig Association as soon as possible.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the leadership that my hon. Friend is demonstrating through the APPG on fisheries for industry and coastal communities like ours. The Government are focused on delivering
deb_ex.sum: Praises the MP's APPG leadership and outlines government support measures for the fisheries sector, committing to further engagement with the APPG on its priorities.

deb_ex.t: we are truly rewiring the state and passing power from the authorities to the hands of ordinary people
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates the Bill as rewiring the state and passing power to ordinary people, credits the Prime Minister for honouring his commitment, and honours the Hillsborough families and wider campaigns including Grenfell and the Primodos families.

deb_ex.t: the campaign for truth and justice does not stop here; indeed, it accelerates from here. I hope it ends the cover-up culture that has failed so many ordinary people
deb_ex.sum: Extends tribute to further groups still seeking justice — treatment disasters, Chinook families, nuclear test veterans — and calls for a special tribunal for veterans, arguing the Bill accelerates but does not end the campaign for truth.

deb_ex.t: Can the Minister confirm whether there have been conversations with European counterparts about applying that flexibility at Dover, Folkestone and St Pancras this summer?
deb_ex.sum: Notes the European Commission's provision allowing member states to partially suspend EES checks at peak times, and asks whether flexibility has been discussed for Dover, Folkestone and St Pancras this summer.
